chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Habib al-Khash'ami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The most preferable among you are those with the best manners, those who are easy to approach, who are familiar and make others familiar, and whose seats are frequently occupied (by guests/friends).'

key_terms.الْمُوَطَّئُونَ أَكْنَافاً: Those who are easy to approach/accommodate

ai.seo_question: What are the key characteristics of the most superior people according to the Prophet in this hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this hadith to emphasize that spiritual excellence is measured by social grace and humility rather than material wealth. The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) specifically praises those who are 'easy to approach' (al-muwatta’ al-aknaf), highlighting the Shia value of *mu’asarah* (good companionship) and the ability to make others feel at ease as key markers of true nobility.
